item.research_question: How do specific alloying elements (Nb, Ta, Ti vs. Cr, Mo) influence the deformation mechanisms and creep resistance of Ni-based superalloys at high temperatures?
item.material_system: Two single-crystal Ni-based superalloys: ME3 (9.1 wt% η phase formers: Nb, Ta, W, Hf, Ti) and ME501 (13 wt% η phase formers), with ME501 having higher Ta, Hf, and Nb and lower Co and Cr compared to ME3.
item.processing_route: Single crystals were cast, heat-treated to form a bimodal γ-γ′ microstructure, and machined into compression cuboids (1:1:2.5 ratio) via Electrical Discharge Machining (EDM).
item.test_conditions: Monotonic compression creep tests at 760 °C on [001] oriented samples; ME3 tested at 414 MPa and ME501 at 552 MPa to achieve comparable strain rates of 5 × 10⁻⁹ s⁻¹.
key_findings: ME501 exhibited remarkably improved creep resistance compared to ME3 at 760 °C and 552 MPa.
Nanotwinning contributed up to 50% of the plastic strain in ME3 but was not operative in ME501.
In ME501, shear-induced solid-state transformation from γ′ to η phase occurred along stacking faults, whereas ME3 showed segregation of γ-formers (Cr, Mo).
Atomic resolution EDX confirmed Ta and Nb segregate to Wyckoff 2a positions and Al and Ti to Wyckoff 2d positions of the η phase at faults in ME501.
The energy barrier for thickening stacking faults into nanotwins was 364 mJ m⁻² for pure Ni₃Al, 481 mJ m⁻² for ME501 (random solid solution), and 743 mJ m⁻² for the η-phase-segregated fault in ME501.
Energy release upon atomic reordering for twin formation was 375 mJ m⁻² for pure Ni₃Al but only 15 mJ m⁻² for ME3.
Isolated stacking faults in ME501 were identified as superlattice extrinsic stacking faults (SESFs) constrained to the γ′ phase.
item.mechanism: The authors propose a 'phase-transformation strengthening' mechanism where high concentrations of η-phase formers (Nb, Ta, Ti) segregate to stacking faults, inducing a shear-induced transformation to a nanoscale η phase. This η phase creates a low-energy structure that significantly increases the energy barrier for the thickening of stacking faults into nanotwins, thereby suppressing the deleterious nanotwinning deformation mode. Conversely, in alloys with γ-formers (Cr, Mo), the fault transforms into a γ-like region that lowers the energy barrier for twin formation.
item.limitations: The text notes that the ability to predict mechanical properties for a given alloy remains a major challenge and that the characterization of specific elements in compositionally complex superalloys has historically been qualitative and empirical.
item.future_work: The authors suggest that this mechanism may be further manipulated through alloying and processing to improve the high-temperature properties of next-generation superalloys for critical structural applications.
quotes: specific alloying elements inhibit the deleterious deformation mode of nanotwinning at temperatures above 700 °C
a superalloy with higher concentrations of the elements titanium, tantalum and niobium encourage a shear-induced solid-state transformation from the γ′ to η phase
